title: Paranormal Activity Turned a $15,000 Budget Into $194 Million
excerpt: ‘Paranormal Activity’ changed the horror genre forever.
content:
Jack Walters

Fri, September 25, 2026 at 1:09 PM UTC

The horror genre has been through so much evolution and reinvention over the decades. Whether it’s Gothic hauntings like Nosferatu, supernatural thrillers like The Exorcist, or juts bloody slashers like The Texas Chainsaw Massacre, there are so many subgenres that have cropped up since the genre was born.

One of the most interesting subgenres, and one that’s only been around for a short amount of time in comparison to the genre’s lifespan, is found footage horror. Thrust into the mainstream by The Blair Witch Project, this subgenre uses low-quality visuals and low-budget production intentionally to create the illusion of being filmed by the characters themselves.

The Blair Witch Project was an enormous success, both critically and commercially, and launched an entire wave of found footage classics throughout the 2000s. The most famous of these was Paranormal Activity.

Directed by Oren Peli, Paranormal Activity was a micro-budget success story that nobody could have seen coming. The film starred unknown actors Katie Featherston and Micah Sloat and follows a young couple who use camcorders to investigate supernatural events that are happening in their home.

The film was made for just $15,000 and ended up returning over $194 million at the box office, making it one of the most profitable films ever made. The huge success of this movie was a tangible turning point for the horror genre—it proved that movies didn’t need huge studios or strong marketing campaigns to become success stories.

Naturally, the huge success of Paranormal Activity meant that sequels were inevitable. Paranormal Activity 2 followed just one year later, although the film is generally seen as a notable step down in quality from the first. Featherston and Sloat returned in their lead roles, with the story jumping between the past and present in an attempt to explain the lore behind these demonic hauntings.

For most fans, the real magic of Paranormal Activity wasn’t the complicated backstory, but rather the simplicity of its shocking scares and chilling performances. This was somewhat lost in the sequel (and subsequent movies in the franchise), which tainted its reputation somewhat. But the fact remains that 2009’s original Paranormal Activity is a strong, captivating piece of horror filmmaking that fundamentally changed the genre forever.
